title: Strontium Ranelate Ameliorates Intervertebral Disc Degeneration via Regulating TGF-beta1/NF-kappaB Axis.
authors: Sun, Ruping; Zhu, Jian; Sun, Kaiqiang; Gao, Lu; Zheng, Bing; Shi, Jiangang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究锶盐对椎间盘退变的治疗作用，涉及TGF-beta1/NF-kappaB信号通路，仅含分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a prevalent and debilitating condition characterized by chronic back pain and reduced quality of life. Strontium ranelate (SRR) is a compound traditionally used for treating osteoporosis via activating TGF-beta1 signaling pathway. Recent studies have proved the anti-inflammatory effect of SRR on chondrocytes. Although the exact mechanism of IVDD remains unclear, accumulating evidences have emphasized the involvement of multifactorial pathogenesis including inflammation, oxidative stress damage, and etc. However, the biological effect of SRR on IVDD and its molecular mechanism has not been investigated. Firstly, this study proved the decreased expression of Transforming Growth Factor-beta 1(TGF-beta1) in degenerated human intervertebral disc tissues. Subsequently, we confirmed for the first time that SRR could promote cell proliferation, mitigate inflammation and oxidative stress in human nucleus pulposus cells in vitro via increasing the expression of TGF-beta1 and suppressing the Nuclear Factor Kappa-Light-Chain-Enhancer of Activated B Cells (NF-kappaB) pathway. The molecular docking result proved the interaction between SRR and TGF-beta1 protein. To further verify this interaction, gain- and loss- of function experiments were conducted. We discovered that both TGF-beta1 knockdown and overexpression influenced the activation of the NF-kappaB pathway. Taken together, SRR could mitigate IL-1beta induced-cell dysfunction in human nucleus pulposus cells by regulating TGF-beta1/NF-kappaB axis in vitro. Finally, the in vivo therapeutic effect of SRR on IVDD was confirmed. Our findings may contribute to the understanding of the complex interplay between inflammation and degenerative processes in the intervertebral disc and provide valuable insights into the development of targeted treatment-based therapeutics for IVDD.
abstract_zh: 椎间盘退变（IVDD）是一种常见且致衰的疾病，其特征为慢性背痛和生活质量下降。雷奈酸锶（SRR）是一种传统上用于通过激活转化生长因子-β1（TGF-beta1）信号通路治疗骨质疏松症的化合物。近期研究已证明SRR对软骨细胞具有抗炎作用。尽管IVDD的确切机制尚不清楚，但越来越多的证据强调了多因素发病机制的参与，包括炎症、氧化应激损伤等。然而，SRR对IVDD的生物学效应及其分子机制尚未被研究。首先，本研究证明了在退变的人椎间盘组织中转化生长因子-β1（TGF-beta1）表达降低。随后，我们首次确认SRR在体外能通过增加TGF-beta1表达并抑制核因子κB（NF-kappaB）通路，促进人髓核细胞增殖，减轻炎症和氧化应激。分子对接结果证明了SRR与TGF-beta1蛋白之间的相互作用。为进一步验证这种相互作用，进行了功能获得和功能丧失实验。我们发现，TGF-beta1的敲低和过表达均影响NF-kappaB通路的激活。综上所述，SRR在体外可通过调节TGF-beta1/NF-kappaB轴减轻IL-1β诱导的人髓核细胞功能障碍。最后，SRR对IVDD的体内治疗效果得到确认。我们的发现可能有助于理解椎间盘中炎症与退变过程之间的复杂相互作用，并为开发针对IVDD的靶向治疗策略提供有价值的见解。
